description: Figure 3 presents two side-by-side bar charts illustrating the relationship between inter-annotator agreement, measured by Fleiss Kappa, and two sample-level ambiguity metrics: ambiguity standard deviation and maximum ambiguity. The left chart plots Fleiss Kappa against four bins of Ambiguity Std (0.0, 0.47, 0.82, 0.94), showing a clear downward trend: agreement is highest (0.88) for samples with zero standard deviation and lowest (0.03) for those with a standard deviation of 0.82. The right chart plots Fleiss Kappa against three bins of Max Ambiguity (1, 2, 3), also showing a decreasing trend: agreement is highest (0.89) for samples with a maximum ambiguity of 1 and lowest (0.23) for those with a maximum ambiguity of 3. Both charts use a vertical y-axis labeled “Fleiss Kappa” ranging from 0.0 to 0.8, and each bar is labeled with its exact Fleiss Kappa value. The figure’s caption explicitly states that it compares inter-annotator agreement to sample-level ambiguity standard deviation and sample-level maximum ambiguity values.
